test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated by the tribal communities of Nagaland and showcases traditional dance and music?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hornbill Festival**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Hornbill Festival** is a major cultural festival celebrated annually in Nagaland, India, by the state’s tribal communities.
 
• It is held from **1st to 10th December** every year at Kisama Heritage Village, near Kohima, the capital of Nagaland.
 
• The festival is organized by the Government of Nagaland to promote and preserve the rich heritage of the state’s **16 major tribes** and numerous sub-tribes.
 
• The event features **traditional dance, music, art, handicrafts, and cuisine**, showcasing the vibrant culture of Nagaland.
 
• It is named after the **Hornbill bird**, a revered symbol in Naga folklore, representing courage and grandeur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tribes of Nagaland:**

 
 
• Nagaland is home to 16 major tribes, including the Ao, Angami, Sumi, Chakhesang, and Lotha tribes, each with distinct traditions, language, and attire.
 
• The tribal communities celebrate many festivals throughout the year, often tied to agricultural cycles.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Hornbill Festival:**
 
 
• It is often referred to as the "**Festival of Festivals**" and serves as a platform to unify the Naga tribes.
 
• The event attracts both domestic and international tourists, boosting Nagaland’s cultural tourism.
 
 
 
• **Kisama Heritage Village:**
 
 
• Kisama is a cultural hub specifically developed to host the Hornbill Festival.
 
• It represents a miniature version of Naga villages, showcasing their architecture and way of life.
 
 
 
• **Hornbill Bird:**
 
 
• The Great Indian Hornbill is a large bird found in the forests of India and Southeast Asia.
 
• It is a recurring motif in Naga folklore and is deeply respected for its majestic appearance.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The festival is an initiative of the Nagaland government to preserve and promote the state’s cultural heritage and to encourage tourism.
 
• It also provides opportunities for artisans and performers to showcase their talent on a global stage.
